title: Ice pile-up against a vertical structure: DEM load history, ISO 19906 benchmark and porosity-resistance scaling

model.contact_law: Fn = min(k_n*delta, sigma_c*h*b(delta)), b = contact chord
model.driving: kinematic platen at drift speed V (far-field ice sheet)
model.boundaries: confining lateral walls, closed downstream end
model.porosity: measured from simulated packing in the window in front of the structure

C3_sigma_c_linearity.criterion: log-log slope of F_max vs sigma_c in [0.75, 1.25] (physical basis of the F = C sigma_c h^2 form)

figures.name: fig1_load_history.png
figures.caption: Load time history on the vertical structure: jam/slip sawtooth of the rubble pile, with the ISO 19906 nominal load and the DEM steady level.

figures.name: fig2_pile_geometry.png
figures.caption: Plan-view floe packing (rubble pile) in front of the structure at the end of a run; dashed purple box = porosity measurement window.

figures.name: fig3_iso19906_comparison.png
figures.caption: ISO 19906 nominal global load compared with the DEM peak and steady loads for the two structure shapes (log scale).

figures.name: fig4_porosity_scaling.png
figures.caption: Steady load versus measured pile solid fraction: log-log fit of F = A (1-n)^alpha (marker size = floe size, colour = friction coefficient).

figures.name: fig5_sigma_scaling.png
figures.caption: Steady load versus compressive strength: the log-log slope tests the linear sigma_c dependence assumed by ISO 19906.
